input:
Write a bash script that summarises an access log.

Starting files:
--- /home/eval/logs/access.log ---
2026-10-01T10:00:01Z GET /api/users 200 12ms
2026-10-01T10:00:02Z GET /api/orders 500 340ms
2026-10-01T10:00:03Z POST /api/orders 201 45ms
2026-10-01T10:00:04Z GET /api/users 200 8ms
2026-10-01T10:00:05Z GET /health 200 1ms
2026-10-01T10:00:06Z GET /api/orders/7 404 5ms
2026-10-01T10:00:07Z DELETE /api/users/3 503 120ms
2026-10-01T10:00:08Z GET /api/users 200 10ms
--- end ---

Each line is: ISO timestamp, HTTP method, path, status code, latency.

The script must:
1. Create /home/eval/reports (it does not exist yet).
2. Write /home/eval/reports/status.txt: one line per distinct status code, formatted `CODE COUNT` (single space), sorted by code ascending.
3. Write /home/eval/reports/errors.txt: for every request with a 5xx status, the line `METHOD PATH`, in log order.
4. Print exactly one line to stdout: `total=<number of requests> errors=<number of 5xx requests>`.
5. Exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

mkdir -p /home/eval/reports

declare -A counts
total=0
errors=0

: > /home/eval/reports/errors.txt

while IFS=' ' read -r timestamp method path status latency; do
  [[ -n "$timestamp" ]] || continue

  total=$((total + 1))
  counts["$status"]=$(( ${counts["$status"]:-0} + 1 ))

  if [[ "$status" =~ ^5[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
    errors=$((errors + 1))
    printf '%s %s\n' "$method" "$path" >> /home/eval/reports/errors.txt
  fi
done < /home/eval/logs/access.log

: > /home/eval/reports/status.txt
while IFS= read -r code; do
  [[ -n "$code" ]] || continue
  printf '%s %s\n' "$code" "${counts[$code]}" >> /home/eval/reports/status.txt
done < <(printf '%s\n' "${!counts[@]}" | sort -n)

printf 'total=%s errors=%s\n' "$total" "$errors"
exit 0
```

input:
Write a bash script that rotates numbered log files.

Starting files in /home/eval/logs (nothing else is in that directory):
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log ---
line c
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.1 ---
line b
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.2 ---
line a
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.3 ---
line 0
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.old ---
manual backup
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/worker.log ---
w2
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/worker.log.1 ---
w1
--- end ---

Define a shell function `rotate LOGFILE KEEP` implementing classic numbered rotation:
- `LOGFILE.N` becomes `LOGFILE.N+1` for every existing N, highest first, so nothing is overwritten.
- Afterwards no numbered file above KEEP may remain (delete any that would end up numbered higher than KEEP).
- `LOGFILE` itself becomes `LOGFILE.1`, and a new empty `LOGFILE` is created.
- Files that are not exactly `LOGFILE` or `LOGFILE.<number>` (for example `app.log.old`) must not be touched.

Then call it twice: `rotate /home/eval/logs/app.log 3` and `rotate /home/eval/logs/worker.log 2`. Exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

rotate() {
    local logfile="$1"
    local keep="$2"
    local path suffix n

    [[ "$keep" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    keep=$((10#$keep))

    # Remove numbered files whose next rotation would exceed KEEP.
    for path in "$logfile".[0-9]*; do
        suffix=${path#"$logfile".}
        [[ "$suffix" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
        n=$((10#$suffix))
        if (( n >= keep )); then
            rm "$path"
        fi
    done

    # Shift remaining numbered files from highest to lowest.
    for ((n = keep - 1; n >= 1; n--)); do
        if [[ -e "$logfile.$n" ]]; then
            mv "$logfile.$n" "$logfile.$((n + 1))"
        fi
    done

    if [[ -e "$logfile" ]]; then
        mv "$logfile" "$logfile.1"
    fi
    : > "$logfile"
}

rotate /home/eval/logs/app.log 3
rotate /home/eval/logs/worker.log 2
exit 0
```

input:
Write a bash script that converts a CSV file to JSON Lines.

Starting files:
--- /home/eval/data/users.csv (no trailing newline on the last line) ---
id,name,email,active
1,Alice Smith,alice@example.com,yes
2,Bob Jones,bob@example.com,no
3,Carol White,carol@example.com,yes
--- end ---

Fields never contain commas or quotes.

Write /home/eval/data/users.jsonl with one compact JSON object per data row (no spaces), in input order, keys in this order: `id` (JSON number), `name` (string), `email` (string), `active` (JSON boolean: `yes` -> true, anything else -> false). Example line: `{"id":1,"name":"Alice Smith","email":"alice@example.com","active":true}`. Every row must be converted, including the last one.

Then print `active=<number of active users>` to stdout and exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

input=/home/eval/data/users.csv
output=/home/eval/data/users.jsonl
active_count=0

: > "$output"
{
  IFS=, read -r header
  while IFS=, read -r id name email active || [[ -n "$id$name$email$active" ]]; do
    if [[ "$active" == yes ]]; then
      active_json=true
      ((active_count += 1))
    else
      active_json=false
    fi
    printf '{"id":%s,"name":"%s","email":"%s","active":%s}\n' \
      "$id" "$name" "$email" "$active_json"
  done
} < "$input" > "$output"

printf 'active=%s\n' "$active_count"
exit 0
```

For every file whose name ends in `.JPG`, anywhere under /home/eval/photos (recursively), rename it in place (same directory) so that its file name is lowercase and every space in the file name becomes `_`. Directory names must NOT change (`Raw` and `Old Shots` keep their names). Other files are left alone. Exit 0.

Write a bash script that renders a config template.

Starting files:
--- /home/eval/app/app.conf.tmpl ---
# generated for ${APP_ENV}
[db]
host = ${DB_HOST}
port = ${DB_PORT}
url = postgres://${DB_USER}@${DB_HOST}:${DB_PORT}/app
[runtime]
home = ${RUNTIME_HOME}
greeting = Hello, ${USER_NAME}!
price = $5 per unit
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/app/prod.env ---
# production settings
APP_ENV=prod/eu
DB_HOST=db.internal
DB_PORT=5432

DB_USER=app_rw
UNUSED_KEY=x
--- end ---

Render /home/eval/app/app.conf.tmpl into /home/eval/app/app.conf:
- `prod.env` holds `KEY=VALUE` lines; blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. Values are taken literally (they may contain `/`).
- Every `${NAME}` placeholder whose NAME is defined in prod.env is replaced by its value.
- Placeholders whose NAME is not defined in prod.env stay exactly as written, even if a variable of that name exists in the shell environment.
- Everything else (including `$5`) is copied unchanged.

Then print one line to stdout: `unresolved: ` followed by the names of the placeholders left unresolved, sorted, unique, space-separated (here: `unresolved: RUNTIME_HOME USER_NAME`). Exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

template=/home/eval/app/app.conf.tmpl
env_file=/home/eval/app/prod.env
output=/home/eval/app/app.conf

declare -A vars=()
declare -A unresolved=()

while IFS= read -r envline || [[ -n $envline ]]; do
  [[ -z $envline || $envline == \#* || $envline != *=* ]] && continue

  key=${envline%%=*}
  value=${envline#*=}
  if [[ $key =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
    vars["$key"]=$value
  fi
done < "$env_file"

render_line() {
  local line=$1 out= tail name char
  local i=0

  while (( i < ${#line} )); do
    if [[ ${line:i:2} == '${' ]]; then
      tail=${line:i+2}
      if [[ $tail == *\}* ]]; then
        name=${tail%%\}*}
        if [[ $name =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
          if [[ ${vars[$name]+defined} ]]; then
            out+="${vars[$name]}"
          else
            out+='\${'"$name"'}'
            unresolved["$name"]=1
          fi
          i=$((i + 3 + ${#name}))
          continue
        fi
      fi
    fi

    char=${line:i:1}
    out+=$char
    i=$((i + 1))
  done

  printf '%s' "$out"
}

: > "$output"
while :; do
  line=
  IFS= read -r line
  status=$?
  if (( status != 0 )) && [[ -z $line ]]; then
    break
  fi

  render_line "$line" >> "$output"
  if (( status == 0 )); then
    printf '\n' >> "$output"
  fi
done < "$template"

unresolved_names=$(LC_ALL=C printf '%s\n' "${!unresolved[@]}" | LC_ALL=C sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
unresolved_names=${unresolved_names% }
printf 'unresolved: %s\n' "$unresolved_names"
```

input:
Write a bash script that creates a small command-line tool and runs it.

No relevant files exist yet; /home/eval/bin and /home/eval/out do not exist.

1. Create the executable script /home/eval/bin/greet (with a `#!/bin/bash` line) that parses options with getopts:
   - `-n NAME`: a name to greet; may be given several times; at least one is required.
   - `-u`: print names in uppercase.
   - `-c COUNT`: repeat the whole greeting COUNT times (default 1); COUNT must be a positive integer.
   - `-h`: print `usage: greet [-u] [-c COUNT] -n NAME...` to stdout and exit 0.
   - Any unknown option, missing option argument, missing `-n`, or invalid COUNT: print that same usage line to stderr and exit 2.
   Output: for each repetition, for each name in the order given, the line `Hello, NAME!`.
2. Then run exactly these commands:
   ```
   mkdir -p /home/eval/out
   /home/eval/bin/greet -u -n alice -c 2 -n bob > /home/eval/out/run1.txt
   /home/eval/bin/greet -n 'Mary Ann' > /home/eval/out/run2.txt
   /home/eval/bin/greet -x -n a 2> /home/eval/out/run3.err; echo $? > /home/eval/out/run3.code
   /home/eval/bin/greet -c zero -n a 2>/dev/null; echo $? > /home/eval/out/run4.code
   /home/eval/bin/greet -u 2>/dev/null; echo $? > /home/eval/out/run5.code
   ```
3. Exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
```bash
mkdir -p /home/eval/bin
cat > /home/eval/bin/greet <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash

usage='usage: greet [-u] [-c COUNT] -n NAME...'
names=()
uppercase=0
count=1

while getopts ':n:uc:h' opt; do
    case $opt in
        n) names+=("$OPTARG") ;;
        u) uppercase=1 ;;
        c) count=$OPTARG ;;
        h)
            printf '%s\n' "$usage"
            exit 0
            ;;
        :)
            printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
            exit 2
            ;;
        \?)
            printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
            exit 2
            ;;
    esac
done

if [[ ! $count =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
    exit 2
fi
count=$((10#$count))

if (( count <= 0 )) || (( ${#names[@]} == 0 )); then
    printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
    exit 2
fi

for ((repeat = 0; repeat < count; repeat++)); do
    for name in "${names[@]}"; do
        if (( uppercase )); then
            name=${name^^}
        fi
        printf 'Hello, %s!\n' "$name"
    done
done
EOF
chmod +x /home/eval/bin/greet
mkdir -p /home/eval/out
/home/eval/bin/greet -u -n alice -c 2 -n bob > /home/eval/out/run1.txt
/home/eval/bin/greet -n 'Mary Ann' > /home/eval/out/run2.txt
/home/eval/bin/greet -x -n a 2> /home/eval/out/run3.err; echo $? > /home/eval/out/run3.code
/home/eval/bin/greet -c zero -n a 2>/dev/null; echo $? > /home/eval/out/run4.code
/home/eval/bin/greet -u 2>/dev/null; echo $? > /home/eval/out/run5.code
exit 0
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
